I have farmed this land since I was a young girl — my mother taught me everything I know. This maize plot is small, only half a hectare, and I plant cowpea between the maize like my neighbors do. Last season I put one full bag of NPK fertilizer on this plot and the maize grew tall, so I will buy one bag again when the agro-dealer comes to the village. I also have goat manure from my animals that I will spread before planting. I keep my own maize seed from last year — I do not trust those new hybrid seeds that cost too much and sometimes fail. I cannot afford chemicals and I do not want them near my food, so my children and I will pull the weeds by hand. We have no water for irrigation here, we only wait for the rains. My sons and daughters will help me clear, plant, weed, and harvest this plot, and I will pay a young man for three days to help with the heavy digging at the start because my back is not strong like before.
